page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-48xCPU-384GB is a memory-optimized virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 48 shared vCPUs powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core performance, as evidenced by stress-ng single-core CPU tests placing in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core execution is robust, with passmark CPU, extended instructions, encryption, and physics tests scoring in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also demonstrates strong performance in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations consistently perform within the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU model offers a lower-cost alternative for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated, continuous single-core compute power. The primary tradeoff is the potential for CPU resource contention due to the shared allocation, making it less suitable for latency-sensitive single-threaded tasks or intensive real-time LLM text generation. This server is best suited for multi-threaded batch processing, memory-cached databases, web serving, and general-purpose workloads requiring substantial memory capacity.
